hook: Ryanair's ticket *doesn't pay* for your flight
paragraphs: Ryanair sells seats from {fourteen euros ninety-nine|€14.99}. Here's the strange part.
In its last full year, the average ticket brought in about {fifty-one euros|€51}. Flying each passenger cost about {sixty-three|€63}.
So on the ticket alone, Ryanair was about {twelve euros|€12} short, for every single passenger.
The difference is the extras you add after you've chosen: a bigger bag, a seat, priority boarding. About {twenty-four euros|€24} per passenger, a third of everything it earns.
Add costs that, by Ryanair's own count, are the lowest in Europe, and about {eleven euros|€11} of profit is left per passenger.
The cheapest seat is rarely why the plane makes money. Full story on the channel.
